requirements.title: Intrinsic and nonintrinsic modules are defined by their source of provision
requirements.definition: An intrinsic module is provided as an inherent part of the processor; a nonintrinsic module is defined by a module program unit or by other than Fortran.

pending.intrinsic-module-processor-provided: Use intrinsic module ISO_FORTRAN_ENV and read INPUT_UNIT into integer observed initialized to -777; assert only that the named constant is accessible as an intrinsic-module entity, not its processor-dependent value.
pending.nonintrinsic-module-program-unit-defined: Define module m1421_nonintrinsic in Fortran with public integer answer=42; client USEs it and expects exact 42 from observed initialized to -777.
pending.nonintrinsic-module-non-fortran-defined: No standard C interoperability mechanism defines a Fortran module. This records processor or build-system latitude for nonintrinsic modules supplied by other means; future tests must use a documented supplied module rather than assuming one exists.

pending.module-implicit-interface-function-expli: Use the same external ABS sentinel with explicit INTEGER type in the module. Source-control mutation removes only the explicit type declaration; no diagnostic is required by this unnumbered restriction.
